body:
I have just uploaded two PR's to first unify 3.x and 4.x BVH. That way we can make subsequent PR's work with both.

See:

#122867
#122869

Is this going to affect physics determinism? Will a scene with the same starting state (including ordering) return the same collision results, or will it be unstable as a result of potential data races? Will there be a way to disable this? What about single-threaded web exports? Wouldn't this reduce performance there?

> Is this going to affect physics determinism? 

Yes, good point, it will affect determinism as written and I think it's worth fixing it to be deterministic. It is valuable to have that, even if it is just to make reproducing bugs more reliable.

> Will a scene with the same starting state (including ordering) return the same collision results, 

Yes, same input and BVH state at the start of the _check_for_collisions() function should create the same **set** of collision results (given exactly the same compiled code). However it will not create the same **order** of collision results unless I make it deterministic (which I will aim to do).

> or will it be unstable as a result of potential data races? 

There is no possibility of data races, unless I have made a mistake. Obviously review and testing is important. 

This is not concurrency style multithreading which has a lot of risks and challenges. This is using multithreading more like SIMD optimisation.

The threading part is just a bunch of worker threads all starting and completing their work within one part of one function `_check_for_collisions_mt()` which waits for them all to complete. There isn't anything running on a background thread.

The worker threads are only able to read state, and I have added 'const' along the path to assure that. However each thread has its own mutable local vector for storing results. I may get slightly more elaborate with the mutable results in order to achieve determinism cheaply, but it will still be relatively simple.

> Will there be a way to disable this? What about single-threaded web exports? Wouldn't this reduce performance there?

This 'broad phase' collision is using Godot WorkerThreads, which are already being used in a similar way in the 'narrow phase' collision and solver within the same physics_step. There is no opt out setting there, so there probably shouldn't be one for this.

If there is only one core, then there will be only one worker available and it will all reduce down to a single loop on the main thread plus some constant set up time (similar to what will happen in the narrow phase collision and solver). The single threaded method already collects results into a LocalVector, so there is negligible difference between the multithreaded path and single threaded.

If I need to add extra work to achieve determinism, then I can do something like: 

```
WorkerThreadPool *pool = WorkerThreadPool::get_singleton();
if(pool->get_thread_count() > 1) {
    // Do determinism stuff or other expensive stuff
}
```

There should be some extra performance headroom in the BVH already from the recent sign bit change, so I can't see this change making anything noticeably slower on any system.

~~I am not sure, but maybe there is a setting somewhere already that limits how many cores can be used by the worker thread system? I think if not, that would be a sensible place to offer control over these sorts of optimisations, and maybe a worthwhile PR in itself.~~

The setting `Threading->Worker Pool->Max Threads` gives the user some control on how much threading is done here and within the physics engine,

I just pushed a commit to add determinism to the worker thread code.

* It outputs the collision results in a deterministic order
* Results ordering should match the output of the single threaded version. 
* Added code is O(n) (added to the O(n) log n collision check)
* Performance seems similar from my profiling, code slightly more complicated.
* If there are less than 2 threads available then the BVH will use the single threaded path. (though this could change)

While the ordering of results is deterministic and matches single player: 
* I don't really have a reasonable way to test this
* I can't say anything for the various numeric functions in the BVH and around it which may affect determinism.
* Switching between the multithreaded pathway and the single threaded pathway based on number of threads could add risk to determinism, so it may not be ideal to soft switch on thread count like this, but rather just use the multithreaded path entirely or single threaded entirely (based on hard template or macro switches).

Note that there is no project setting that entirely works to turn off BVH worker threading in 4.x (at least partly due to this crash: #123413). However you can turn off threads altogether with the `threads=no` option on an `scons` build of the engine.
